seoTitle: Hair Salon & Barbershop Google Maps & Local SEO
description: Local SEO for hair salons and barbershops: Google Maps ranking, Google Business Profile, categories, posts, reviews and booking-page tips, in reading order.
intro: This guide covers how hair salons and barbershops get found on Google Maps and in local search. It includes full local SEO guides, Google Business Profile optimization, choosing categories, using profile posts, review benchmarks, a city example and website pages that turn visitors into bookings. It is for salon and barbershop owners who want more people to find and book them without paying for ads.

With limited money, start with your Google Business Profile: correct categories, hours, services, photos and a booking link. Then read the local SEO guide for your business type and work on collecting reviews steadily. After that, improve your website booking page and add regular profile posts. These steps cost mostly time and tend to build over weeks and months.

Most of this is manageable on your own if you can set aside a few hours a month. Help can be worthwhile when you are in a crowded city, your listing has problems you cannot trace, or you simply have no time between clients. DataLatte offers local SEO support, but the guides here explain the essentials.

faq.q: How do I rank higher on Google Maps as a hair salon?
faq.a: Start by completing your Google Business Profile with accurate categories, services, hours and photos. Then earn reviews steadily, keep your name, address and phone consistent across the web, and make your website clear about what you offer and where. Rankings take time and are never guaranteed.

faq.q: Which Google Business Profile category should a barbershop choose?
faq.a: Choose the primary category that best describes your main service, and add secondary categories only where they truly apply. Our categories article explains the options for salons, and the same logic applies to barbershops. Review it periodically as Google updates its list.

faq.q: How many Google reviews does a salon need?
faq.a: There is no magic number. What matters is having a healthy count compared with nearby competitors, recent reviews and thoughtful replies. Our Denver benchmark article shows how to compare yourself with local rivals.

faq.q: Do Google Business Profile posts help salon bookings?
faq.a: They can help keep your listing active and show offers, new services or openings to people who find you. They are unlikely to transform rankings alone. Treat them as a small, regular habit alongside reviews and good photos.
